limitations: binding is to Secure Boot POLICY STATE (PCR7); /boot and the ESP are unencrypted and are NOT measured, so an attacker who boots a signed live environment (Secure Boot still enabled, PCR7 unchanged) could replace the initramfs with one that exfiltrates the LUKS key and then let the TPM release it on the next boot

Fedora GRUB permits editing a boot entry at the menu unless a superuser password is set, so rd.break or init=/bin/bash can yield a root shell on the already-unlocked volume with no passphrase and with PCR7 unchanged

the safe statement is therefore: recovery from power loss is fully automatic, at the cost of theft-resistance for an intact stolen machine; disk-only theft remains protected because the TPM is on the motherboard

mitigations, cheapest first: grub2-setpassword; firmware password and restricted removable boot; revoke the OpenAI key and bot token on theft; clevis/tang or the UKI/signed-PCR11 phase for the real fix
PCR7 can move on Secure Boot key/database/MOK changes or firmware updates, requiring supervised re-enrollment
the SER3 uses a firmware TPM (MSFT0101), weaker than a discrete TPM
auto-unlock leaves the dm-crypt key in RAM while running, so cold-boot and DMA attacks on a running or suspended machine become newly relevant
discard remains in the crypttab options and was deliberately preserved
